source_name: EUR-Lex — Czech-language official texts of EU financial-services law (CELEX by document)
why_relevant: Authoritative, legally binding Czech-language version of every EU regulation/directive that binds Czechia (PSD2, IPR 2024/886, DORA 2022/2554, MiCA 2023/1114, AMLR 2024/1624). Carries entry-into-force and date-of-application articles verbatim, plus consolidated versions and corrigenda that shift deadlines.

source_name: EUR-Lex — Official Journal L series, daily editions (CS)
why_relevant: The moment of publication in the OJ starts every EU deadline clock. Daily L-series monitoring is the earliest reliable trigger for new delegated/implementing regulations (RTS/ITS) under PSD2, DORA, MiCA and the IPR.

source_name: ČNB — DORA: Digitální provozní odolnost finančního trhu (thematic hub)
why_relevant: ČNB's national landing page for Regulation (EU) 2022/2554: scope in CZ, reporting obligations, register of information submission deadlines, webinars and slide decks that state exactly what CZ entities must file and when.

source_name: ISAP — Informační systém pro aproximaci práva (Úřad vlády ČR)
why_relevant: The government's own EU-to-CZ implementation tracker: assigns the responsible ministry ('gestor') for each EU act, records transposition method, transposition deadline, and compatibility of draft CZ law with the EU act. This is precisely where an EU deadline becomes a Czech legislative task, and it covers acts long before ČNB says anything.

source_name: EBA — Regulation and policy / Single Rulebook (incl. Interactive Single Rulebook and Q&A)
why_relevant: Source of the level-2/level-3 material (RTS, ITS, guidelines, Q&As) that determines what PSD2/PSR, DORA and AMLR actually require operationally. EBA publishes guidelines in all EU languages including CS, and the Q&A answers are what CZ-supervised PSPs are held to.

source_name: EBA — Compliance tables for guidelines (national competent authority compliance status)
why_relevant: For each guideline EBA publishes a compliance table naming which NCAs comply / intend to comply / do not comply, and from when. This is the EU-side mirror of the ČNB 'Sdělení' and lets you detect CZ divergence or delay without waiting for ČNB.

source_name: EBA — Consultations / public hearings (open consultation register)
why_relevant: Earliest visibility of future binding technical standards under PSR/PSD3, DORA and AMLR — typically 2-3 months of comment window, with the final text landing 6-12 months later. Gives lead time no CZ-only source offers.

source_name: EBA — Payment Institutions Register (PSD2) and Credit Institutions Register (EUCLID)
why_relevant: EU-level consolidated register fed by ČNB notifications; lets you see CZ-authorised PSPs/EMIs and their passporting footprint (~199 CZ entries reported), and detect authorisation-regime changes as PSD3/PSR re-license the population.

source_name: European Commission — Have Your Say (public consultations & feedback portal)
why_relevant: Upstream of everything else in this cell: call-for-evidence and consultation windows (4-12 weeks) for PSD3/PSR follow-ups, retail payments, digital euro, AML implementing acts. Available in CS interface for many initiatives, and CZ stakeholder submissions are published, revealing national positions.

source_name: European Commission DG FISMA — banking and finance regulation pages
why_relevant: Owner of PSD3/PSR, IPR and the AML package; publishes the political-agreement announcements, adopted delegated acts and application-date explainers that fix the timetable CZ entities must plan against.

source_name: ECB — Instant Payments Regulation / retail payments pages
why_relevant: Explains IPR obligations and their staggered dates, including the distinct, later timetable for non-euro-area Member States such as Czechia (euro instant payments obligation for CZ banks reported from July 2027, euro payments from koruna accounts from June 2028). That CZ-specific offset is the single most consequential deadline in this cell.

source_name: ČNB — CERTIS / okamžité platby (instant payments) pages
why_relevant: The CZ national counterpart to the IPR: CERTIS is the domestic instant-payment rail, and ČNB has publicly reasoned about not joining TIPS. Changes here signal how Czechia will actually meet the EU euro-instant obligation (correspondent access vs. direct TIPS participation).

source_name: FAÚ (Finanční analytický úřad) — AML balíček / AML nařízení section
why_relevant: The CZ FIU is the national authority for the EU AML package. Its AMLR/AMLD6 pages carry the Czech reading of Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 and its 10 July 2027 application date, plus methodological guidance banks and PSPs will be judged against.

source_name: Ministerstvo financí ČR — Finanční trh / konzultační materiály
why_relevant: MF ČR is the gestor for transposing EU financial-services directives (PSD3, AMLD6) and runs national consultation rounds ('konzultační materiál') on how to exercise Member State options. It authored zákon o digitalizaci finančního trhu (31/2025 Sb.) implementing MiCA/DORA. This is where the CZ national application choices are decided.

source_name: NÚKIB — cybersecurity authority statements on DORA/NIS2 overlap for financial entities
why_relevant: DORA (EU) meets the CZ zákon o kybernetické bezpečnosti (NIS2 transposition). ČNB and NÚKIB have issued a joint interpretation of which obligations apply to DORA entities under ZKB — a CZ-only resolution of an EU-law boundary question that no EU source contains.

source_name: International law-firm PSD3/PSR trackers (Norton Rose Fulbright, Morrison Foerster, Freshfields, HSF Kramer, Worldline)
why_relevant: PSD3/PSR is still pre-publication; these trackers are currently the most granular public reconstruction of the trilogue outcome, scope and the entry-into-force + 18/21-month application arithmetic that will determine the CZ deadline. Replace with EUR-Lex CS text the moment the OJ publication lands.

source_name: EUR-Lex — Legislative summaries in Czech (souhrny právních předpisů EU)
why_relevant: Official Commission-authored plain-Czech summaries of SEPA/payments and other acts. Excellent for building the CZ glossary (nařízení, směrnice, úhrada, inkaso, poskytovatel platebních služeb) and for quickly scoping an act before reading the binding text.

source_name: ČNB SDAT — reporting platform, DORA register-of-information section
why_relevant: Where the abstract EU obligation becomes a dated filing: taxonomies, submission windows and technical specifications for the DORA register of information that CZ financial entities must send to ČNB. Deadline changes surface here first and are machine-checkable.

source_name: Finanční analytický úřad (FAÚ) — official site root
why_relevant: Primary Czech FIU and AML/CFT + sanctions supervisor for banks and payment institutions; the site is the hub from which all metodické pokyny, stanoviska, sanction pages, risk assessments and annual reports branch. Snowballing this root yields the whole cell.

source_name: FAÚ — Metodické pokyny (methodological guidelines index)
why_relevant: Canonical numbered guidance series (MP č. 1 sanctions/TF, č. 3 beneficial owner, č. 4 STR reporting, č. 5 restrictive measures, č. 6 gambling, č. 7 PEP, č. 8 ID copying, č. 9 kontrola klienta, č. 11 risk assessment + internal rules). These directly define onboarding, KYC and monitoring system requirements for banks and payment providers, and FAÚ enforces against them in inspections.

source_name: FAÚ — Stanoviska FAÚ (binding-in-practice opinions, by topic)
why_relevant: Topic-sorted interpretive opinions (obecná stanoviska, oznámení kontaktní osoby, identifikace klienta, kontrola klienta, vysoce rizikové třetí země, skutečný majitel, mlčenlivost, PEP, oznamování podezřelých obchodů). Faster-moving and more operationally granular than the metodické pokyny — the best early signal of shifting supervisory expectations.

source_name: FAÚ — Mezinárodní sankce (international sanctions hub)
why_relevant: FAÚ's sanctions branch: aktuálně o sankcích, sankce v ČR, legislativa a metodika, informační zdroje, plnění oznamovací povinnosti, výjimky ze sankcí, žádost o vynětí. This is the authority-side definition of screening, freezing and reporting duties for payment providers.

source_name: FAÚ — Aktuality (news / notices feed)
why_relevant: Fastest-moving FAÚ channel: new guidance announcements, high-risk third country list updates, deadline reminders (e.g. contact-person notification deadlines), sanctions notices. This is the natural trigger stream for a deadline tracker.

source_name: FAÚ — Právní předpisy (legal acts index for AML/sanctions)
why_relevant: Curated list of the applicable legal base (AMLZ 253/2008 Sb., sanction acts 69/2006 Sb. and 1/2023 Sb., EU regulations). Serves as the authoritative mapping from 'obligation' to 'statutory provision', which anchors deadline and obligation extraction.

source_name: FAÚ — Výroční zprávy (annual reports)
why_relevant: Quantified supervisory activity: number and type of inspections of obliged entities (incl. banks, payment institutions, VASPs), administrative proceedings, fines, sanction-list screening findings, STR volumes. This is the single best indicator of where FAÚ enforcement pressure is heading, and it names the shared-supervision split with ČNB.

source_name: FAÚ — Hodnocení rizik / Národní hodnocení rizik (NRA) and risk-trend reports
why_relevant: National ML/TF risk assessment rounds (2nd round public version published; 3rd round in progress) plus the first proliferation-financing NRA and 'Zprávy o vývoji rizik'. NRA outputs feed directly into what FAÚ expects in an obliged entity's own hodnocení rizik under MP č. 11 — i.e. they pre-announce future inspection focus.
